claims.statement: tests/test_alignment_rust_parity.py is the contract test file that enforces parity between the pure-Python SmithWatermanAligner and the Rust-backed RustSmithWatermanAligner (cite_right._core extension), asserting that align_citations can substitute one backend for the other without behavior change.

The contract is enforced on three Rust entry points: align_pair_details (6 integers plus match count), align_pair_blocks_details (same plus match_blocks for multi_span_evidence=True), and align_best_details (7-element tuple selecting across a candidate list with deterministic tie-breaking).

The tuple shapes compared element-for-element are: align_pair_details returns (score, token_start, token_end, query_start, query_end, matches); align_pair_blocks_details returns those six followed by match_blocks as a list of (token_start, token_end) runs in seq2; align_best_details returns (score, index, token_start, token_end, query_start, query_end, matches), or None for an empty candidate list.

When two alignments have the same score, the Python and Rust backends must agree on which one is best, in this priority order: higher score, higher matches, smaller token_start, larger span length (token_end - token_start), smaller query_start, smaller original index in the candidate list, then token_end and query_end as final tie-breakers.

test_rust_parity_for_equal_score_more_matches_case pins the equal-score coverage regression: when two cells have the same score, the one with more matches must win, and the Rust traceback must agree with Python. The canonical regression sequences are seq1=[0,1,0] and seq2=[0,1,1,1,0], and the test is gated on requires_rust_blocks because it uses align_pair_blocks_details and the Python aligner with return_match_blocks=True.

Tests skip cleanly when the Rust extension is missing or out of date via two pytest markers and two fixtures defined in tests/conftest.py: requires_rust skips if cite_right._core cannot be imported; requires_rust_blocks additionally skips if _core does not expose align_pair_blocks_details; the rust_core and rust_core_with_blocks fixtures return the imported module or skip with the corresponding reason.

The RustSmithWatermanAligner constructor performs a construction-time check that the relevant _core entry points exist: when return_match_blocks=True it requires align_pair_blocks_details and align_batch_blocks_details, otherwise it requires align_pair_details and align_batch_details, and raises RuntimeError with a rebuild message if any is missing, so a mismatched extension fails fast rather than silently producing empty evidence_spans.

The test_rust_block_and_non_block_entrypoints_share_alignment test pins the invariant that the choice of alignment does not depend on whether match_blocks are being collected: align_pair_blocks_details and align_pair_details on the same input must agree on the first six tuple elements, and only the match_blocks element is allowed to differ.

test_rust_align_best_empty_returns_none pins the contract that align_best and align_best_details return None (not an empty tuple, not a crash) when the candidate list is empty, and align_batch must preserve input order from the candidate list to the returned list of Alignment objects.
